title: Frobenius Generates the Cyclic Galois Group of a Finite Field
description: For a finite field K of characteristic p, with prime subfield 𝔽_p = ZMod p and degree n = [K : 𝔽_p] (so |K| = p^n), the Galois group Gal(K / 𝔽_p) = K ≃ₐ[ZMod p] K is cyclic of order n, generated by the prime Frobenius x ↦ x^p. The Frobenius has order exactly n: its n-fold iterate x ↦ x^(p^n) = x is the identity, but no smaller positive power is. Culminates in an explicit group isomorphism Multiplicative (ZMod n) ≃* Gal(K / 𝔽_p). Answers OQ-01 of the parent Frobenius entry. 10 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.

overview.historicalContext: The Galois theory of finite fields is the cleanest non-trivial example of the Galois correspondence: for every prime power q = p^n there is, up to isomorphism, a unique field 𝔽_q, and its Galois group over the prime field 𝔽_p is cyclic of order n, generated by the Frobenius automorphism x ↦ x^p. This single fact underlies the classification of finite fields, the structure of their subfields (in bijection with divisors of n), and the local theory of number fields and function fields. The parent entry exhibited the Frobenius as an endomorphism; here it ascends to an automorphism and the generator of the Galois group.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (OQ-02, Frobenius endomorphism)**: Exhibit the iterated Frobenius x ↦ x^(p^k) as a generator of Gal(𝔽_{p^n} / 𝔽_p), with order exactly n; record that the n-fold iterate returns the identity and assemble the cyclic structure of the Galois group.

**Formalized**: frob (the Frobenius as an element of Gal(K/𝔽_p)) and frob_apply (it is x ↦ x^p); orderOf_frob and card_galoisGroup (order n); zpowers_frob_eq_top, mem_zpowers_frob, exists_pow_frob (it generates); frob_pow_finrank, frob_iterate_finrank, frob_pow_ne_one (order exactly n, n-fold iterate is the identity); and galoisGroupMulEquivZMod (the explicit isomorphism Gal(K/𝔽_p) ≅ ℤ/n).
overview.text: A 123-line formalization upgrading the Frobenius endomorphism of the parent entry to the Galois-theoretic setting. For a finite field K of characteristic p, with prime subfield 𝔽_p = ZMod p, the Frobenius x ↦ x^p is realised as an element frob of the Galois group Gal(K/𝔽_p) = K ≃ₐ[ZMod p] K (frob_apply confirms it acts as x ↦ x^p). The group is cyclic (isCyclic_galoisGroup) of order n = [K : 𝔽_p] = log_p |K| (card_galoisGroup), and frob has the same order (orderOf_frob), hence generates the whole group (zpowers_frob_eq_top, mem_zpowers_frob, exists_pow_frob). The order is exactly n: the n-th power is the identity automorphism (frob_pow_finrank), equivalently the pointwise iterate x ↦ x^(p^n) = x (frob_iterate_finrank), while no positive power below n is (frob_pow_ne_one). The entry culminates in an explicit isomorphism Multiplicative (ZMod n) ≃* Gal(K/𝔽_p) (galoisGroupMulEquivZMod). All results verified with 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.
overview.proofStrategy:
**The Frobenius as an automorphism**: frob is FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic (ZMod p) K, the |𝔽_p|-power automorphism. Because |𝔽_p| = Fintype.card (ZMod p) = p, frob_apply (rw ZMod.card) identifies it with the honest prime Frobenius x ↦ x^p.

**Order and cyclicity**: orderOf_frob is FiniteField.orderOf_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic (= Module.finrank); isCyclic_galoisGroup is Mathlib's IsCyclic Gal(L/K) instance for finite fields; card_galoisGroup is IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank, the IsGalois and FiniteDimensional instances being automatic for finite extensions.

**Generation**: zpowers_frob_eq_top rewrites with Subgroup.card_eq_iff_eq_top, Nat.card_zpowers (Nat.card ⟨frob⟩ = orderOf frob), orderOf_frob and card_galoisGroup to match |⟨frob⟩| = |Gal|; mem_zpowers_frob and exists_pow_frob then follow (the latter via mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers in the finite group).

**Order exactly n**: frob_pow_finrank is pow_orderOf_eq_one after rewriting orderOf_frob; frob_iterate_finrank chains coe_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_iterate (iterate is x ↦ x^(p^n)) with pow_finrank_eq_card (p^n = |K|) and FiniteField.pow_card; frob_pow_ne_one uses orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one and omega.

**Structure theorem**: galoisGroupMulEquivZMod transports zmodCyclicMulEquiv (Multiplicative (ZMod (Nat.card G)) ≃* G for cyclic G) along card_galoisGroup.
keyInsights: **The prime base collapses the abstract Frobenius to x ↦ x^p**: Mathlib's frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic is the |base|-power map; over 𝔽_p the base has exactly p elements, so the Galois generator is literally the parent entry's endomorphism — the automorphism and the endomorphism are the same map, now invertible.

**Order = dimension = generator**: the three quantities orderOf(frob), Nat.card Gal(K/𝔽_p), and Module.finrank (ZMod p) K all coincide with n. Equality of the first two is exactly what forces ⟨frob⟩ = Gal(K/𝔽_p): an element whose order equals the group's cardinality generates.

**n-fold iterate is the identity, and not before**: frob^n = 1 because x^(p^n) = x^|K| = x for every x; frob^m ≠ 1 for 0 < m < n because otherwise X^(p^m) − X (degree p^m < |K|) would have all |K| elements as roots. This is the 'order exactly n' that the parent OQ asked for.

**Explicit cyclic structure**: rather than merely asserting cyclicity, galoisGroupMulEquivZMod produces a concrete isomorphism Gal(K/𝔽_p) ≅ ℤ/n sending the additive generator 1 to the Frobenius — the full structure theorem, from which the lattice of intermediate fields (subgroups of ℤ/n, i.e. divisors of n) reads off immediately.

conclusion.summary: Upgrades the Frobenius endomorphism x ↦ x^p of a finite field K (parent entry) to an element frob of the Galois group Gal(K/𝔽_p), proves that group cyclic of order n = [K : 𝔽_p] with frob as a generator (zpowers_frob_eq_top), records that the order is exactly n — the n-fold iterate x ↦ x^(p^n) = x is the identity (frob_iterate_finrank) and no smaller positive power is (frob_pow_ne_one) — and culminates in an explicit isomorphism Multiplicative (ZMod n) ≃* Gal(K/𝔽_p). 10 theorems and 2 definitions, 0 sorries and 0 axioms, no native_decide.
conclusion.implications: The cyclic structure Gal(𝔽_{p^n}/𝔽_p) ≅ ℤ/n, with the Frobenius as canonical generator, is the foundation of the Galois theory of finite fields: intermediate fields correspond to subgroups of ℤ/n, i.e. to divisors of n, giving the subfield lattice 𝔽_{p^d} ⊆ 𝔽_{p^n} ⇔ d ∣ n. The Frobenius is also the local model for the Frobenius elements of global Galois groups in algebraic number theory, where this cyclic picture governs the splitting of primes.
